subject: Educational software about simplest population dynamics

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Educational software about simplest population dynamics
parts:
Dear group,

 

this is perhaps a somewhat off-topic question, but I ask anyway. --- With a colleague we have been musing about the interest to educate the public about basic processes underlying population dynamics, e.g., how things like (initial) population size and the BIDE rates affect outcomes like population trajectories and extinction probabilities and how factors such as (for instance) hunting or wind turbines  on the one hand, or habitat or population management can affect all of these.

 

We were first thinking about physical models, e.g., using balls in an urn, but I think this is too limited. So the obvious choice is some computer model of a population, where BIDE rates can be specified. Ideally, we’d have some GUI where the user could use a slide bar to set the desired values for the BIDE rates and then there would be one or more plots, e.g., of the trajectory of a single population or of the cluster of such trajectories to show the uncertainty arising from variability or a histogram of final population sizes including an estimate of extinction probability.

 

I bet somebody has already coded up such solutions and hence, rather than re-invent the wheel, we’d be happy to hear about anything you might know of (or have programmed yourself).

 

Thank you and best regards  ---- Marc

messages.author: 14db3d7db7d740a2
messages.subject: Re: Educational software about simplest population dynamics
parts:
Hi Marc,

This past spring I was looking for a similar tool for teaching an undergraduate population ecology class. I ended up coding several mini web applications using R and Shiny, which is simple to do and allows you to create something customized to your needs. For example, I wrote this app (https://amtucker.shinyapps.io/wild4890_pred_prey/) to have students explore predator-prey dynamics. This app (https://amtucker.shinyapps.io/wild4890_pva/) sounds close to what you are looking for, but it was designed to teach about conducting demographic PVAs and the types of uncertainty involved, so it might contain more detail than you need. You are welcome to use it, and I'm also happy to send along the source code, which is just R wrapped in some special functions to create the web interface. 

I hope this helps!
Anna



Anna Tucker
PhD Candidate
School of Forestry and Wildlife Sciences
Auburn University
annamtucker.weebly.com

messages.author: e52aff30a33f7a8a
messages.subject: Re: Educational software about simplest population dynamics
parts:
Hi Marc et al.,

Similarly, the Zipkin lab at MSU developed this shiny app (https://danaus.shinyapps.io/Danaus/) to (hypothetically) demonstrate how varying environmental/habitat factors could impact the monarch butterfly population size in the future. It uses exactly what you mention - a slider bar - to set desired values for each management scenario, and the code is provided on the right-hand side of the interface. We developed it for an outreach event for Girls Math and Science Day (6th - 8th graders) to get young women excited about coding and ecology! 

Hope this helps - and feel free to email the main developer, Alex Wright (adwr...@msu.edu), with any questions.

Best,
Sarah

parts:
That is great stuff and should be used much more than just publishing equations.

Another software package that can perform such interactive demonstrations that runs locally (on PC, Mac, and Linux platforms) is Mathematica (Wolfram, Inc.).  Here is an example:  http://demonstrations.wolfram.com/PredatorPreyDynamicsWithTypeTwoFunctionalResponse/.  Attached is a screenshot.


To view such demonstrations it takes a free CDF (computable document format) reader but to buy Mathematica to build such apps is not cheap.  The advantage is that the app runs locally on your machine and can be very responsive. 

Jim Baldwin

Hi Marc,

 

This past spring I was looking for a similar tool for teaching an undergraduate population ecology class. I ended up coding several mini web applications using R and Shiny, which is simple to do and allows you to create something customized to your needs. For example, I wrote this app (https://amtucker.shinyapps.io/wild4890_pred_prey/) to have students explore predator-prey dynamics. This app (https://amtucker.shinyapps.io/wild4890_pva/) sounds close to what you are looking for, but it was designed to teach about conducting demographic PVAs and the types of uncertainty involved, so it might contain more detail than you need. On Wednesday, August 29, 2018 at 3:53:32 AM UTC-5, marc.kery wrote:

Dear group,

 

this is perhaps a somewhat off-topic question, but I ask anyway. --- With a colleague we have been musing about the interest to educate the public about basic processes underlying population dynamics, e.g., how things like (initial) population size and the BIDE rates affect outcomes like population trajectories and extinction probabilities and how factors such as (for instance) hunting or wind turbines  on the one hand, or habitat or population management can affect all of these.

 

We were first thinking about physical models, e.g., using balls in an urn, but I think this is too limited. So the obvious choice is some computer model of a population, where BIDE rates can be specified. Ideally, we’d have some GUI where the user could use a slide bar to set the desired values for the BIDE rates and then there would be one or more plots, e.g., of the trajectory of a single population or of the cluster of such trajectories to show the uncertainty arising from variability or a histogram of final population sizes including an estimate of extinction probability.

 

I bet somebody has already coded up such solutions and hence, rather than re-invent the wheel, we’d be happy to hear about anything you might know of (or have programmed yourself).

 

Thank you and best regards  ---- Marc
